content.thinking:
I'm planning to write the whole file carefully in one pass, keeping it robust with simple geometric primitives, lathe and extrude shapes, and SVG textures. I'm sketching the bookshelf dimensions—about 2 meters tall, 1.3 wide, 0.4 deep, standing on the ground facing forward—and considering whether the builder requires a root joint.

I'll create a root joint at the origin so every part attaches to it, and use flat colors sparingly while relying on paint textures for the wood grain. Then I'm defining helper functions for parts and sketching the structure: base plinth and feet, side panels, back panel, five evenly spaced shelves, and a decorative crown on top using a combination of boxes and extruded gable shapes.

For materials, I'm leaning toward rich walnut wood with gold trim and a teal arcane glow accent, applying grain textures through cel-shaded paint with the grain axis adjusted per part orientation. Now I'm thinking through how to build books for the shelves—spine boxes, inset page blocks, gold banding—designed to face forward with visible spines.

Working out the book geometry: instead of a solid cover with hidden pages, I'll construct it from a front spine plate plus two thin side boards with a pages box sandwiched between, so the pages peek out visibly at the top edge like a real book.

With around 6 parts per book across ~30 books plus gold spine bands, I need to watch the overall part budget of 1000, so I'll keep band counts shared or minimal rather than adding too many extras.

For spine decoration, rather than modeling text I'll use a simple plane with an SVG texture for labels or runes, reusing just a few texture variants to save on draw calls.

Now I'm working out the shelf layout: computing board center heights and thicknesses so compartments between them come out to roughly 0.4 units tall each, with side panels spanning the full interior height.

For depth placement, I'm positioning the back panel and front edges so books sit properly within the shelf depth. Then I start planning the bottom shelf's contents — stacked horizontal tomes with a chained book on the left side.

Now I'm laying out the top shelf: flat stacked books topped with a skull and candle on the left, tall standing books in the center, and a glowing orb on a brass stand with a ring on the right. For the shelf below, I'm placing a varied row of books on the left and a scroll rack with horizontal cylinders in the center.

For the pile of scrolls, I'm arranging small cylinders in a pyramid shape with a ribbon band wrapped around them, plus leaning books and potion bottles on the right. The next shelf gets a trio of colored glowing orbs on pedestals alongside books and candles, and the bottom shelf gets a full row of books, a hourglass, and an owl figurine built from spheres with glowing eyes.

I'm designing a reusable candle component with a wax-dripped cylinder body, visible wick, a teardrop-shaped glowing flame made from layered cone and sphere shapes, and a small gold holder dish underneath.

For the orb, I'm sketching out a gold claw-footed stand holding a glowing sphere with a brighter inner core and a white highlight, plus a thin orbiting torus ring around it. I'm also planning glowing rune-carved plane decals on the side panels to add some magical detail.

Now I'm moving on to the front corner posts—turned gold baluster-style columns with a lathe profile that flares at the base and capital, giving a classic furniture-leg look at the front corners.

Then I'm adding gold accent trim: slender strips along each shelf's front edge, and a decorative gabled cornice at the top built from an extruded polygon outline to create a peaked, molded crown shape.

For the gable I'm positioning the depth and thickness so it sits properly at the front face, painting it in the wood tone. For the glowing crescent moon on the gable, I'm working out the geometry by computing a crescent shape from two overlapping circles -- one outer arc and one offset inner arc -- to carve out the familiar moon sliver silhouette.

I realize I had the direction backwards—the crescent opening toward +x needs the inner arc to trace the left side of the inner circle, the part that actually sits inside the outer disk, not the rightmost bulge which falls outside the outer circle entirely.

Now I'm tracing the polygon boundary: outer arc runs from 55.3° around through 180° to 304.7°, then the inner arc connects back from 278.6° through 180° to 81.4°, closing the loop while dropping the duplicate endpoint vertices so the shape doesn't double up at the seams.

I want the crescent horns pointing upward rather than opening to the right, so I'm rotating all the generated points 90° counterclockwise by swapping and negating coordinates.

Now I'm thinking the crescent could cradle a glowing orb inside it, like a cute little scene. I'll also add a small owl made of around 12 parts (body, head, glowing eye decals, ear cones, wing boxes, beak, feet) positioned top right, plus floor props like stacked tomes, a tall melted candle holder, and a leaning scroll bundle to extend the scene's footprint.

Overall width with floor items comes to about 2.0 and height 2.4. For texturing, I'm planning parchment labels with rune variants, and deciding between cel-shaded painting for larger surfaces like wood cabinets and floor stacks versus flat solid colors for smaller items like book spines, keeping a limited palette of around 12 colors to manage texel density within the paint sheet budget.

I'm tallying up the color count across all painted elements—books, pages, gold trim, glow effects, candles—landing around 35, which should be fine for a standard shaded box material. I'm also confirming that wood grain painting works correctly on box UVs before setting up a seeded RNG for variation and starting to scaffold the builder code with joint roots, part helper functions, and proper typing for colors and paint fills.

Setting up builder scaffolding...

For tilted books, I'll handle the leaning rotation by computing local offsets then transforming them around a pivot point at the base, writing a small helper to convert local coordinates into world positions.

Defining book geometry with spine, boards...

Still positioning labels and bands...

For flat lying books, I'm thinking through the construction: top and bottom cover plates sandwiching a slightly inset pages block, with the page edges peeking out at the sides to suggest a stack of paper between the covers.

Now I'm working out the yaw rotation math so each book can be rotated about the Y axis around its own pivot, letting me stack several flat books at different angles with gold accent details on top.

Finishing the frame helper...

Designing SVG textures for the labels, rune glow columns on the sides, and the orb glow effect...

Writing candle geometry function...

For the flame I'm layering a cone for outer orange glow with a smaller yellow cone inside. For the hourglass, I'm designing it with two cone-shaped glass bulbs, wooden caps, connecting posts, and a sand fill, using a pale blue glass color and a lathe-based profile for the bulb shape.

Defining lathe profile points...

I'm sketching the gold crown-like lathe profile for the pedestal top, then adding a seat ring and orbit ring using torus geometry rotated flat. For the orb itself I'm layering in a swirling smoke effect with offset bright spheres and a highlight, maybe adding sparkle accents too.

Now I'm thinking through building paper scrolls -- cylinders for the paper body oriented along different axes depending on placement, with wooden roller knobs at the ends and a ribbon band wrapped around using a torus, adjusting rotation based on whether the scroll lies horizontally or vertically.

I'm also working out the shelf geometry for the cubby storing the scroll pile, calculating board centers, thicknesses, and top surfaces to figure out compartment heights between shelves.

I'm now planning out vertical dividers and the contents for each shelf by x-position, starting with a stack of three tomes with varying thickness and yaw on the first shelf.

Continuing this, I'll place a candle on top near the stack, then a run of eight standing books with varying widths and heights leading to a tilted bookend, and finally a globe on a stand positioned at the right side of the shelf, checking that its radius keeps it under the shelf height above.

For the second shelf, I'm laying out seven books along the left side, then a scroll cubby in the middle with divider panels and a pyramid stack of scrolls arranged so their circular ends face the viewer, working out radius and spacing to fit the available width.

Checking the total scroll width fits within the inner divider span, confirming the center position aligns correctly, and deciding to skip ribbon bands in favor of colored spiral caps for simplicity, noting torus geometry defaults to z-axis orientation so no extra rotation is needed.

For the right side of the shelf, I'm placing three glowing potion bottles at varying heights and colors plus a tilted book. Then for the third shelf, I'm laying out three small orbs on pedestals at different x positions with teal, violet, and amber colors, each topped by a hanging star accent.

For the center-right section I'm arranging a cluster of leaning books with a candle holder perched on two flat stacked books, saving a hourglass placement for the next shelf. On shelf four, I'm placing a row of books on the left with one tall tome, an hourglass near the center, and considering a small vase with a rolled scroll bundle to fill out the remaining space.

The vase holds five tilted scroll cylinders rising above its rim, while on the right I'm stacking three flat books topped with a tiny inkpot and a quill made from a thin tilted rod with a tapered cone acting as the feather vane.

For the top of the structure, I'm adding a cornice with a gable featuring a moon and glowing orb, plus candelabra at both ends made from lathe-turned stands with small candles positioned symmetrically along the cornice top, and I still need to place an owl figure near there.

I'm working out the owl's exact position relative to the gable's sloped outline so it reads as sitting on the cornice without being awkwardly clipped by the gable's front face, testing a few x/z offsets to get the depth layering right.

Now I'm placing the shelf decorations on the left side — stacked books with a candle, another candle grouping near the owl, and figuring out the gable's centerpiece with a crescent moon, an orb nestled in it, and surrounding stars.

Working out the crescent moon's exact position and extrusion depth so it sits flush against the gable's front face without clipping through it.

For the gable's decorative trim, I'm defining the outline as a series of points along the roofline and plan to run gold rods between successive points to form the border edge.

I'm now adding gold trim strips along the shelf fronts, side panel details with wood grain and edge rods, and designing a back panel painted as a starry night sky using a cell-based noise pattern for the stars against a deep indigo background.

Still placing plinth moulding and checking clearances against side panels, then adding turned corner posts at the front edges with gold-colored lathe segments.

I'm keeping the post shaft a darker wood tone with gold torus rings at the base and capital, topped with a finial sphere, and confirming the posts' height tucks neatly under the cornice band at the top.

Now building the cornice itself with a layered wood box, a thin gold trim strip, and a row of small dentil boxes positioned so they sit just under the shelf without clipping into it -- I'll merge those dentils into a single geometry using BufferGeometryUtils for efficiency.

For the floor, I'm placing a large pillar candle with wax drips on an iron stand near the left side, plus a round rug positioned in front to anchor the composition without overcrowding the space.

Now placing floor decor on the rug: a tall stack of five flat books near the right side, a floor candle on the left, and skipping extra clutter like orbs or cauldrons to keep things simple. I'm adding a woven scroll basket at the front-right with several scroll rods tilted and sticking out of it.

Before writing code, I'm double-checking the API details: using the lathe and extrude builder functions with proper bone support and bevel constraints, and remembering that glow effects need plain string colors rather than Paint objects, especially when combined with textured parts like runes.

Now I'm setting up the colored texture plane for the books and planning out a palette of rich jewel-tone colors for the book spines, plus gold, pages, wax, and flame colors for the finishing details.

I'm also thinking through the wood grain shading for shelves—using a celshaded grain paint with different axes for light and dark wood tones—and deciding that books will stay flat-colored while boards get a slightly darker shade, with gold accent bands. Now I'm starting to define the function that builds a standing row of books.

Writing row-placement logic...

Now I'm estimating total part counts across shelves to stay under a reasonable complexity budget—roughly 650 total pieces including bands and labels, well under the 1000 limit.

Starting the implementation now...

I confirm INK is used for the wick color, then start building the default export function, setting up the builder and root joint, and defining helper functions like `put` and `box` for constructing geometry parts.

Still writing helpers...

Still writing book geometry...

Still writing flat book geometry...

Writing candle geometry function...

Adding inner flame glow and drip details...

Now I'm shaping the orb with a lathe profile and double-checking the outline doesn't self-intersect, then adding a cradle ring with torus geometry and small claw prongs to hold the orb in place.

Adding highlight spheres and a darker orbit ring to give the orb surface depth and dimension...

I'll skip the decal/swirl texture idea since it's too risky, and instead move on to designing the potion shape with its glowing lathe body, cork, and a labeled band wrapped around it.

Now I'm refining the lathe outline for the potion bottle, shaping the neck and shoulder curve with explicit coordinate points, then adding a small cork cylinder at the top. Next I'm sketching the hourglass object with wooden end caps.

I realize the glass being opaque would hide the sand entirely, so I decide to skip the sand detail and just use a pale teal glass color with a subtle glow. Now I'm shifting to designing the vase shape itself, sketching out a lathe profile with widening and narrowing curves to give it a ceramic silhouette.

Next I'm adding decorative elements: scroll rods angling out from the vase top with paper-colored caps and small knob spheres, plus a gold band torus accent on the vase body. Then I move on to sketching the owl figure—a purple-brown body ball scaled for shape, with a lighter belly and head sphere positioned above it.

Basket gets a woven stripe pattern with slight wobble for texture, plus scroll-like rods for handles. Now I'm defining a radial paint function for the rug, using distance and angle from a center point to create concentric colored rings.

Still writing rug rings...

Still placing decorative elements, working out the left panel orientation, merging the dentil boxes into one geometry, and adding glowing gold stars near the moon on the gable before moving on to the gold mouldings on the front.

Rather than a candle, I'll add a tiny glowing mushroom cluster instead, building each one from a stem cylinder and a hemisphere cap with tiny white spot balls, colored pink, and placing a trio on one of the shelves.

Now I'm working out the exact positions for the shelf objects—stacked books, small orbs, and the mushroom cluster—making sure they fit within each shelf's width without overlapping. I'm writing a helper function that generates rows of books with randomized widths, heights, and colors using a seeded random generator, so each shelf looks varied but reproducible.

For the leaning last book in a row, I'm adjusting its x-position and depth so it tilts against its neighbors convincingly, aligning book backs along a consistent z-plane while letting depth vary slightly per book for a natural, uneven look.

I'll settle on x + 0.19*h for the lean offset. Now I'm working through each shelf row's item counts and widths to check that totals stay within bounds—shelf2's row of about 6-7 items ending near the divider, shelf1's standing row of 6 items landing around 0.30, and checking the orb at 0.45 doesn't overlap given its radius—adjusting counts where rows would run too long.

For shelf3's row from -0.1 with 6 items plus lean, it ends around 0.38, keeping clear of the mushrooms starting at 0.45. Shelf4's left row similarly ends near -0.1, so I'm placing the hourglass at x=0, the vase at 0.2, and trimming the stack's flat length to 0.26 at x=0.45 so it stays within the 0.585 boundary instead of overflowing.

I'm also pinning down the left stack on shelf1—centering it around x=-0.37 with depth 0.26 and back-aligning its z position—then setting height ranges per shelf (roughly 0.3-0.4 for shelf1, 0.26-0.36 for shelves 2 and 3, 0.26-0.34 for shelf4) before placing the divider boxes on shelf2 at x=-0.045 and x=0.305.

Now I'm working out the shelf1 candle stack's total height by stacking the base thickness, candle body, and flame to confirm it stays under 0.6, then designing a floor pillar candle with an iron lathe-profile stand and a tall wax cylinder with drips and an enlarged flame, checking its top reaches about 0.74. I'm moving on to position a floor stack on the right side near x=0.92, z=0.05.

Writing label SVG strings...

Still drafting glyph shapes...

Writing rune glow SVG...

Now I'm designing the mushroom shape with a tan stem, pink glowing dome cap, and white spots positioned using trig to sit correctly on the cap's curved surface.

Then I'm adding the owl's purple wizard hat with a brim and gold band, followed by the owl's body geometry — scaled spheres for the body and belly positioned with offsets for a rounded, layered look.

Still writing owl head details...

Still placing hat details and candles...

I need to be careful with TypeScript typing throughout — making sure coordinate arrays and outline points get the right tuple types so the lathe and extrude functions accept them without inference errors, annotating explicitly where needed before writing the actual file.

Now I'm mapping out the gable's edge rods, tracing the outline polygon counterclockwise from the base corners up through the peak points so each top edge segment gets a correctly positioned rod.

Placing the rods and moon at slightly different z-depths, then working out post positions so they hug the panel's front corners with proper ring details.

Now I'm positioning the shelf's front gold trim strips flush against the board's front face, checking depth overlaps with the back panel dimensions.
